questions.question: Which length instruction is the most reliable?
options: Give exactly 5 bullets, one line each
Be as concise as an expert would be
questions.explanation: Countable units such as words, bullets, or sections remove guesswork. Vague words like "brief" mean different things to different readers.

questions.question: You want plain paragraphs with minimal formatting, but your prompt is a long bulleted Markdown spec. What is likely to happen?
options: The model will always ignore the prompt's own formatting
The model will refuse to answer
The output tends to mirror the prompt and come back as bulleted Markdown
The model will switch to JSON automatically
questions.explanation: Prompt style influences output style. Reducing formatting in your own prompt helps get less formatted output.

questions.question: Why might a reply drafted with Markdown headings and double-asterisk bold look wrong when pasted into an email?
options: Email clients automatically translate Markdown into another language
Markdown makes the email longer than the word limit
Email servers reject messages containing asterisks
Many email clients do not render Markdown, so the symbols appear literally
questions.explanation: Destinations differ: many email clients and WhatsApp do not render standard Markdown, so you should name the destination and ask for suitable formatting.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop the model adding "Sure, here is your summary!" before output you plan to paste into a CRM?
options: Explicitly ask for only the output (for example, only the filled template) with no preamble or explanation
Ask for the answer in bullets
questions.explanation: Telling the model exactly what to output, and what to leave out (preambles, explanations, alternatives), keeps the result paste-ready.
